messages:
mia_support: Heads-up: NimbusAnalytics (tenant:nimbus-123) opened an escalation — p99 token latency jumped ~3x over the last 2 hours, customers seeing timeouts. They repro consistently on long-context chat sessions. Logs indicate GPU memory pressure and a sequence of allocator OOM / KV growth logs. Escalating to runtime + infra.
sam_oncall: Ack. I see the alert group for us-west2. Can you paste the sample request and the logs you have? Also how widespread is this (single pool / tenant)?
mia_support: Single tenant, single dedicated pool (pool-id d-54). Sample request: POST /v1/generate with ~6k token context, temperature 0.2, max_tokens 1024, batch_size=1. Repro script attached below.
alex_support_engineer: Repro script (sanitized):
```
for i in {1..20}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-xl-13b","input":"<~6k tokens>","max_tokens":1024}' &
done
```
mia_support: Logs (excerpt):
```
[2026-03-16T09:12:01Z] runtime: gpu0: allocate slab failed: OOM (requested 268435456)
[2026-03-16T09:12:01Z] runtime: kv_store: tenant=nimbus-123 kv_bytes=3.9GB kv_items=12842
[2026-03-16T09:12:02Z] allocator: compact_slab triggered, reclaimed 32MB
[2026-03-16T09:12:05Z] runtime: retrying request, fallback path, latency=2.1s
[2026-03-16T09:12:08Z] runtime: p99 latency spike: 3400ms
```
sam_oncall: That kv_bytes looks high for a single tenant on that pool. Is KV eviction disabled or tuned low? Also any recent model or rollout changes on d-54?
joey_runtime: No rollouts scheduled. We're seeing a correlated KV growth pattern: long contexts + repeated generation bad for prefix caching + absent aggressive eviction leads to growth and fragmentation on GPU allocator. Two short mitigations to try immediately:
  1) Reduce per-tenant concurrency to 2 for d-54
  2) Lower prefix cache window for the tenant (prefix_cache.max_entries=500)
lee_infra: I can throttle concurrency and push a config change. Which flag do you want? Also we can enable slab compaction more frequently: allocator.compact_interval from 300s -> 60s as a surgical mitigation.
sam_oncall: Apply both: throttle concurrency + more frequent compaction. Also temporarily disable prefix KV caching for that tenant if possible.
alex_support_engineer: Pushed: tenant.throttle=2, prefix_cache.max_entries=500. Scheduler applied to nodes in pool d-54. Leaving prefix cache on for now; can flip if no improvement. 
ci-bot: Deploy initiated by lee_infra at 2026-03-16T09:22:10Z — rolling config update across d-54 (10 nodes)
joey_runtime: In parallel, try a runtime allocator tweak: enable aggressive_slab_compaction=true and set allocator.slack_pct=5 for this pool. This reduces fragmentation at the cost of slightly higher CPU.
lee_infra: I can flip aggressive_slab_compaction on d-54 now. Any expected side effects to alert on?
joey_runtime: Watch p50 latency and CPU of runtime pods. Expect small CPU uptick, p50 stable. We want p99 down and fewer OOM logs.
sam_oncall: Also adding an automatic fallback policy: if gpu_oom_count > 3 in 5m then route new requests to a smaller variant (quantized) for the tenant.
mia_support: Sent mitigation steps to the customer; they confirmed they see reduced errors after a couple minutes. Current metrics:
```
before: p99 = 3400ms, gpu_oom_rate=0.9/min
after: p99 = 1250ms, gpu_oom_rate=0.15/min
```
alex_support_engineer: Good improvement. Still above SLO. Joey, what's a medium-term fix? Allocator rework? KV eviction policy change?
joey_runtime: Medium-term: two-pronged approach:
  - implement per-tenant soft-KV quotas (stop unbounded kv growth)
  - tune the allocator to use larger super-slab compaction windows and reduce small-slab blowups (flag: allocator.ballast_ratio)
  - also consider offloading cold KV entries to host DRAM (hybrid KV tiering)
lee_infra: Per-tenant soft quotas will require schema change in KV meta; estimate 2-3 sprints. We can prioritize a targeted mitigation: enable hybrid KV tiering per pool (moves least-recently-used items to CPU memory) — that might be a 1-week effort to test.
sam_oncall: For now, keep the concurrency cap and compaction changes for 24 hours, collect heatmaps, and run a thorough repro test (20 parallel long-context requests). Alex, can you coordinate a staged repro with the customer during low-impact window?
alex_support_engineer: Will coordinate with Nimbus for a 30-min window at 18:00 PST and run the 20-request repro. Will post heatmaps + allocator logs back here.
ci-bot: Alert: packer job for allocator-ballast experiment scheduled (non-prod) 2026-03-17T02:00Z
mia_support: Customer wants ETA on a permanent fix — quoted: "we'll schedule hybrid-kv tiering and per-tenant quotas in the roadmap; tentative ETA 4-6 weeks." They accepted the workaround for now.
joey_runtime: One more immediate tweak we can try if p99 creeps back: reduce generation window (max_tokens) per request via an enforcement rule for the tenant. e.g., max_tokens=512. That reduces KV churn significantly.
lee_infra: Noted. I will also add a short-term dashboard to track: kv_bytes, gpu_oom_rate, allocator_frag_pct, p99_latency for d-54 / tenant nimbus-123.
sam_oncall: Thanks everyone. Keep this thread updated with the repro results and heatmaps. If we hit >3 OOMs in 10m again, escalate to on-call infra immediately.
alex_support_engineer: Repro completed at 2026-03-16T18:32Z — attached heatmap shows KV growth plateau after compaction. Will upload logs in support ticket and update the customer.
mia_support: Customer confirmed lower error rate overnight. Closing for now; leaving ticket open for follow-up on the roadmap items. Final notes: immediate mitigations = concurrency throttle + aggressive compaction; medium term = hybrid KV tiering + per-tenant KV quotas + allocator tuning.
